item.text: I’m checking a small set of primary and high-authority sources to verify whether the 2024 macro turn actually left Turkey on a better trajectory, and to capture the main counterevidence on inflation, living standards, and policy fragility.

item.text:
Provisional read: **mixed, slightly positive on macro trajectory, but not on lived outcomes**. In 2024, Erdoğan’s team did execute a real stabilization turn under heavy external constraints, yet inflation stayed high, living standards remained strained, and some policy choices still looked politically managed rather than broadly corrective.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Turkiye: 2024 Article IV Mission Press Release | IMF | 2024-08-28 | [link](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/08/28/pr24311-turkiye-2024-article-iv-mission-press-release) | IMF staff said the policy turnaround since mid-2023 sharply reduced crisis risks, raised confidence, lifted reserves, and set up 2024 growth around 3.4% while inflation, though still high, had started to ease. This is strong evidence of a more competent trajectory than the inherited macro mess. | 5B.10; also 5B.9, 5B.7 |
| Positive | Republic of Türkiye: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director | IMF | 2024-10-11 | [link](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/11/republic-of-trkiye-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-556139) | The IMF said tighter policy reduced macro imbalances, revived confidence, and lowered inflation, while also warning that significant external and financial vulnerabilities remained. This supports a partial improvement, not a full turnaround. | 5B.10; also 5B.9, 5B.7 |
| Positive | Press Release on Interest Rates (2024-01) | Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye | 2024-01-25 | [link](https://tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/en/tcmb%2Ben/main%2Bmenu/announcements/press%2Breleases/2024/ano2024-01) | The central bank raised the policy rate to 45% and explicitly cited sticky domestic demand, services inflation, and geopolitical risk, while also noting improving inflation expectations, stronger reserves, and current-account rebalancing. That is evidence of real stabilization policy under external pressure. | 5B.10; also 5B.9, 5B.7 |
| Positive | Annual Gross Domestic Product - 2024 | TURKSTAT | 2025-09-01 | [link](https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/en/press/54187) | TURKSTAT reported that annual GDP increased 3.3% in 2024. Even with severe inflation, the economy still expanded, which supports the argument that the year ended on a somewhat stronger output path than the inherited crisis baseline. | 5B.10; also 5B.9 |
| Negative | Dark days for Turks as Erdogan atones for economic errors | Reuters | 2024-07-18 | [link](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/dark-days-for-turks-as-erdogan-atones-for-economic-errors-2024-07-18/) | Reuters described eroding living standards, years of punishing inflation, and a sharp credit clampdown. This cuts against any claim that the improved macro line had yet translated into broad economic relief for households. | 5B.10; also 5B.9, 5B.7 |
| Negative | Shock, confusion as Turkey seizes earthquake survivors' homes | Reuters | 2024-03-18 | [link](https://www.reuters.com/commodities/shock-confusion-turkey-seizes-earthquake-survivors-homes-2024-03-18/) | Reuters reported deed transfers in Hatay to the Treasury under an urban-planning amendment, alarming survivors. That is a major property-rights and trust shock that weakens the “stronger trajectory” reading, especially in a disaster-hit region. | 5B.10; also 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9 |
| Negative | Turkey to lift minimum retirement pay, impose minimum corporate tax | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-07-16 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/turkey-to-lift-minimum-retirement-pay-impose-minimum-corporate-tax/2176793/) | Reuters portrayed the minimum-pension increase as targeted relief in an inflationary environment, not as a broader structural fix. That looks more like political management of pain than durable improvement in the economy’s trajectory. | 5B.10; also 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.9 |
| Negative | Turkey’s revolving door: Five years, six central bank chiefs | Reuters | 2024-02-05 | [link](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Turkey-s-revolving-door-Five-years-six-central-bank-chiefs-45882771/) | Reuters highlighted the revolving-door history at the central bank and said Erdoğan had fired the last four governors, which had badly damaged credibility. That undermines the case for durable, institutionally grounded recovery. | 5B.10; also 5B.7, 5B.9 |

Search gap: I found strong evidence on inflation, reserves, growth, and crisis management, but much less direct 2024 evidence on unemployment, public debt, or sanctions-specific effects. Those dimensions are mostly only inferable from the IMF’s broader warnings about energy prices, capital flows, and geopolitical tensions rather than from Turkey-specific labor/debt datasets in 2024.
